# API Mock Services

> Stand-ins for the outside world. One implementation, shared: the payment
> gateways, identity checks, email, DNS, messaging, AI and storage a project
> talks to in a test — running locally, offline, with no dependencies.

Repository: https://github.com/omeiza-workspace/api-mock-services
Package: `@bytesickle/api-mock-services` (npm)
Licence: MIT

## What this is

A set of mock HTTP servers that answer like the real provider does, and
remember what they were asked. They run in a Node test, in a container, or
over HTTP for a project in any language.

18 mocks: stripe, resend, xero, cloudflare, paystack, interswitch,
youverify, onesignal, twilio, flutterwave, monnify, termii, smileid,
identitypass, whatsapp, fcm, openai, s3.

## Install

```sh
npm install --save-dev @bytesickle/api-mock-services
```

There are no runtime dependencies. Node 20 or newer.

## Use it in a test

```js
import { startMock } from '@bytesickle/api-mock-services'

const stripe = await startMock('stripe')

process.env.NUXT_STRIPE_API_BASE = `${stripe.url}/v1`

// ... the test ...

expect(stripe.last().path).toBe('/v1/refunds')
expect(stripe.state.refunds[0].payment_intent).toBe('pi_test_1')

await stripe.close()
```

## The command line

```
api-mock-services list                    # what there is, by category
api-mock-services start stripe resend     # start some (one process, many ports)
api-mock-services env                     # the environment for the whole stack
api-mock-services file ./mocks/acme.json  # a mock written as a route file
api-mock-services pay stripe failed       # the next payment fails
api-mock-services error stripe server     # the next call answers 500
api-mock-services webhook stripe resend   # send the webhook again
api-mock-services reset stripe            # forget everything
api-mock-services logs stripe             # watch the requests
```

The control surface is `/_control` on every mock. The panel is `/_panel`.

## Layout

```
src/harness.js     the engine — routes, state, the control surface. No HTML.
src/index.js       the public API
src/spec.js        a mock written as a route file
src/providers/     the mocks, one file per group of them
src/ui/            the browser layer: templates/, assets/
```

`src/ui/` is separate from the engine on purpose. The engine never imports
the UI; the UI is attached with `attachViews(service)`.

## Conventions for contributors

- No new dependencies. Node is the whole toolchain, including the lint
  (`npm run lint`) and the footprint budget (`npm run footprint`).
- The real shape: the paths, fields and status codes are the provider's.
- Keep the state: what was asked and what was decided lives on
  `service.state` and `service.requests`.
- The reference decides: a reference containing `success` succeeds, one
  containing `failed` fails.
- A provider that wants a checkout declares `service.checkout = { title,
  find, onDone }`; it must not import the UI.
- Every mock is registered in `src/index.js` with a port, a category and a
  description, and has a test in `test/`.

## Commands

```sh
npm test           # the tests (node --test)
npm run lint       # the house style
npm run check      # both
npm run footprint  # the memory, CPU and startup budget
make ci            # the tests, then the CI kit gate
```

Architecture notes: https://github.com/omeiza-workspace/api-mock-services/blob/main/ARCHITECTURE.md
